description: The state space already contains a 3-dimensional object, Sym^2(V), but it fails the Sym^2 gate because all SU(2) reps are self-dual; hence no summand of any V^(tensor n) can pass. Bean qou-8p1i.

computation.arithmetic: exact integer weight multisets; no floating point

data.verdict: a 3-dimensional object exists natively (Sym^2(V), the SU(2) adjoint) but fails the Sym^2 gate: Sym^2(3) = 5+1 has a singlet because the adjoint is self-dual, whereas SU(3)'s Sym^2(3) = 6 is irreducible
data.generalisation: CORRECTED 2026-08-07. Self-duality alone does NOT decide the gate: for the SU(2) irrep of dimension d the invariant form is symmetric when d is odd (singlet in Sym^2, gate fails) and antisymmetric when d is even (singlet in Lambda^2, gate passes). What holds is: no ODD-dimensional SU(2) irrep passes the gate, in particular none of dimension 3
data.superseded_claim: an earlier version asserted 'every summand of every tensor power is self-dual, so none can pass the gate'. That is FALSE -- the 2-dimensional fundamental is self-dual with FS = -1 and PASSES the gate (C3 of this module is the counterexample to the generalisation it was used to support). The downstream conclusion is unaffected because it only needs dimension 3
data.scope: scope-(b) for 'some ODD-DIMENSIONAL summand of V^(tensor n) with dim V = 2 passes the Sym^2 gate', excluded by the Frobenius-Schur parity computation (C6), NOT by self-duality alone. Even-dimensional summands are symplectic and do pass the gate; they are the wrong dimension for a triplet
data.consequence_for_T3b: 'inequivalent fibre objects' cannot mean different summands of V^(tensor n); it must mean genuinely non-isomorphic fibres, a Tannakian gerbe / multi-fibre-functor situation
not_claimed: that no 3-dimensional fibre exists anywhere in the framework -- only that it is not inside the tensor powers of the existing 2-dimensional one
anything about how to construct inequivalent fibres
